::: {#thm-normal-vector-uphill}

#### The normal vector points uphill

Let $\modmemf{\vx} = \dprod{\vcoef}{\vx} + \coef{0}$ with $\vcoef \neq \vzero$.

1. For every $\vx \in \reals^p$ and $t \in \reals$, $\modmemf{\vx + t\vcoef} = \modmemf{\vx} + t\norm{\vcoef}^2$.
2. Among [unit vectors](linear-algebra-vectors.qmd#def-unit-vector) $\vu$ ($\norm{\vu} = 1$), the change $\modmemf{\vx + t\vu} - \modmemf{\vx}$ with $t > 0$ is largest for $\vu = \vcoef / \norm{\vcoef}$.

:::

::: proof
**Part 1.**
By linearity of the [dot product](linear-algebra-vectors.qmd#def-dot-product),

$$
\begin{aligned}
\modmemf{\vx + t\vcoef}
&= \dprod{\vcoef}{\vx + t\vcoef} + \coef{0} \\
&= \dprod{\vcoef}{\vx} + t\dprod{\vcoef}{\vcoef} + \coef{0} \\
&= \modmemf{\vx} + t\norm{\vcoef}^2.
\end{aligned}
$$

**Part 2.**
For a [unit vector](linear-algebra-vectors.qmd#def-unit-vector) $\vu$,

$$
\modmemf{\vx + t\vu} - \modmemf{\vx} = t\dprod{\vcoef}{\vu}.
$$

Since $t > 0$, maximizing this change is the same as maximizing $\dprod{\vcoef}{\vu}$.
By the [Cauchy-Schwarz inequality](linear-algebra-inner-products.qmd#thm-cauchy-schwarz), $\dprod{\vcoef}{\vu} \le \norm{\vcoef}\norm{\vu} = \norm{\vcoef}$.
Equality holds exactly when $\vu = \alpha\vcoef$ for some $\alpha > 0$.
The condition $\norm{\vu} = 1$ then forces $\alpha\norm{\vcoef} = 1$, so

$$
\vu = \vcoef / \norm{\vcoef}.
$$
:::
